title: Relief Limits Across All Plans on a Loan — Hardship Assistance Programs
content:
Relief on one loan under the Hardship Assistance Programs is limited across all of its plans.

## 1. Lifetime deferral limit

Over the life of a loan at most 6 installments may be deferred, counting every program that defers installments; a deferral request is offered only for as many installments as remain under that limit. The count is every installment recorded as deferred on that loan, under any hardship plan. Disaster Relief deferrals count toward this lifetime limit.

## 2. Rolling 24-month relief limit

The months of plans whose program counts toward the relief limit may cover at most 12 loan due dates in the 24 calendar months ending on the new plan's first affected due date, and a counting plan is offered only for the months that fit. The months counted are the loan due dates inside that 24-month window that fall between the start date and the end date (inclusive) of each plan on the loan whose program counts toward the relief limit and that became active (has an acceptance date), whatever its later status. Disaster Relief Deferral and Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit never count toward the 24-month relief limit.

## 3. Uses, spacing and the wait after a broken plan

A program may be used on a loan no more often than its maximum uses per loan, and a new plan of the same program may start only once its minimum months between uses have passed since the earlier plan of that program ended. A use is a plan of the same program on the loan that became active. After a plan on the loan is broken, a new request (other than Disaster Relief Deferral or Servicemember Rate Cap Benefit) is taken only after the broken program's wait has passed. The request fits the program's lifetime uses, its spacing since the previous plan of the same program, and the wait after any broken plan on the loan. This is judged on the company's records of the plans on the same loan — their program, status, acceptance date and closing date — before the request is taken.

The per-program figures (whether a program counts toward the relief limit, its most uses per loan, its months between uses and its wait after a broken plan) are those of the program's usage-limit register.

## 4. When a limit leaves no room

When a limit leaves no room, the request is declined with the reason "relief limit reached".

## Hypothetical cases

- A loan with 5 installments already deferred under earlier plans asks for a 2-installment deferral: 1 installment remains under the lifetime limit, so the deferral is offered for 1 installment.
- A loan whose counting plans already cover 10 due dates in the 24 months ending on the new plan's first affected due date has room for 2 more; a counting plan is offered only for the months that fit.
- A plan that became active and was later broken still has its due dates counted in the 24-month window; a plan that was only offered and expired never became active and is not counted.
